NEGROES BLOCK PASSAGE OF WHITES AT HEFLIN
Heflin, Aug. 1.—(Special.)—Is it believed that the presence of extra police alone prevented a race riot at the depot here last night.

Several thousand negroes have been in Heflin attending a district conference. Many of them were leaving here Sunday night and they and their friends so blocked the passage to the train that it was impossible for white passengers to get aboard the cars.

Lem Heard, a Heflin negro was knocked senseless, and the services of a physician were required to restore him to consciousness. It is said that he was asked to make room for others. and refused to do so. The deputies then began using their clubs.

The situation is much more quiet today, and it is believed that there will be no further trouble.

thomas-pollard-richmond-1910-08-21.A1:
NEGRO RESISTS ARREST,
IS SHOT BY POLICEMAN
IS SHOT BY POLICEMAN
Threats Made Against Officer and Armed Squad Goes to His Aid.
Special Dispatch to The Star.
Special Dispatch to The Star.

RICHMOND, Va., August 27.—In the heart of the negro section of the city tonight Policeman Perkinson shot and instantly killed Thomas Pollard, colored.

Immediately following the killing the negroes made threats, and Perkinson, one of the coolest men on the force, stood his ground. News of the affair was phoned to the station, and a squad of men in the automobile patrol were rushed to the scene. The officers were armed with automatic riot guns, and were under orders to shoot. The presence of the policemen soon sufficed to restore quiet.

Had Engaged in Pistol Duel.

Pollard and another negro had engaged in a pistol duel in the street, and when the policeman attempted to arrest him Pollard seized the policeman's club and struck him a powerful blow on the head. The officer then pulled his revolver and shot Pollard.

Soon after the shooting an immense crowd collected, and for half an hour the situation was threatening. Perkinson has been placed under arrest and has been balled for his appearance in court.

The coroner will hold an inquest tomorrow.
thomas-pollard-richmond-1910-08-21.A2:

OFFICER KILLED
VICIOUS NEGRO

Perkinson Forced to
Shoot to Resist Attack
by Pollard.

POLICE QUICKLY
DROVE MOB AWAY

Arrival of Squad With Riot Guns
Quelled Disturbance in Jack-
son Ward—Fight in Woman's
House Between
Brothers Led to Assault
on Perkinson.
While trying to capture two brothers who were in a desperate fight over a woman, Policeman W. J. Perkinson, attached to the Second Police Station, shot and killed Relford Pollard, colored, thirty-four years old, last night about 7:30 o'clock at 1018 St. Peter Street, after the negro had resisted arrest. With a bullet wound through his lungs, Pollard leaped a fence and fell dead.

When Policemen Perkinson and Walker, who had been dispatched from the Second Police Station to quell a row in a house at 1018 St. Peter Street, reached the door they heard a shot fired. Breaking open the door, the two officers found two negroes fighting for possession of a pistol. Seeing the policemen, both men fled. Officer Walkes ran after Tom Pollard, and Officer Perkinson followed Relford Pollard.

Stunned Before He Shot.

Dashing into the yard, with Officer Perkinson close to his heels, Relford Pollard twisted a paling from a fence and struck the policeman on the head and again on the limbs. Perkinson was stunned for an instant, but whipping out his pistol, fired at the negro, who ran, leaped a fence and staggered a short distance, where he sank to the ground mortally wounded.

Patrolman Walker chased Tom Pollard for some distance, as he scaled fences and darted through dark alleys, finally making his escape. Tom Pollard made no effort to resist arrest, but took to his heels as if he were making a dash for his life.

In two or three minutes after the shooting more than 1,000 negroes filled the streets and alleys around the yard where the trouble had occurred. Other officers, attracted by the shots, came running through the streets in an effort to locate the disturbance.

Riot Guns Rushed to Scene.

Some one telephoned to the Second Police Station that a negro had been killed and unless a squad of police were hurried to the scene it was feared there would be a clash between the officers and the negroes. Sergeant Otey sent Sergeant Neisz, Officers Krinkle, Tiller, Atkinson, Thurman, Samuels, Flournoy, Smallwood and Allen with riot guns.

Major Werner was immediately notified, as was Captain Epps, in charge of the Second Police Station. Major Werner and Captain Epps communicated with several officers, including Detective-Sergeants Wren and Wiley, who picked up several others, and armed them with riot guns, and proceeded to St. Peter and Hickory Streets, Major Werner, with a squad of men, and Captain Epps, with another, soon reached the scene of the trouble, where they found hundreds of negroes arguing, cursing and making a lot of talk. When they saw the policemen coming with the riot guns they quickly dispersed.

Fought to Get Pistol.

Mazie Robinson, the woman about whom the Pollard brothers engaged in a desperate combat, does not know which one fired the pistol. She told the police that Tom and Relford Pollard were in her house to see her; that they quarreled and then leaped at each other. In a hand to hand struggle a shot was fired, and the woman said she could not tell by whom. She believed that the two men were fighting to gain possession of the pistol.

An instant after the weapon was discharged the two policemen rushed into the house, which was filled with smoke. The brothers separated, and one ran one way and one the other, with the policemen chasing them. It was in the yard that Relford Pollard assaulted Officer Perkinson with the paling, after which he was killed.

Perkinson Arrested.

Sergeant Neisz, after making an investigation of the shooting, promptly swore out a warrant for Policeman Perkinson, and he was arrested on a formal charge of murder. He was taken to the Second Police Station, where Judge Witt placed him under a bond of $1,000 pending the coroner's inquest.

Coroner Taylor was summoned and after examining the body of Pollard, ordered it sent to Undertaker Johnson's on Foushee Street. Dr. Taylor said that the bullet entered the negro's right side near the back and passed through the lungs.

The post-mortem examination will be held this morning at 10 o'clock. The inquest will be held to-morrow at 10 o'clock, when the police hope to have captured Tom Pollard.

Tom Pollard an Ex-Convict.

Several detectives were detailed last night by Major Werner and Captain Epps to search the city for Tom Pollard. Both Pollard negroes bear a bad reputation. According to their father, who lives at $87 North Seventh Street, Tom has only recently served a term in the penitentiary. The old man said that Relford went to West Virginia about the time his brother was sent to prison and he remained there until Tom got out of the penitentiary, when he returned to Richmond, and the brothers have been "bumming around" together ever since.
thomas-pollard-richmond-1910-08-21.A3:
THOMAS POLLARD
FINALLY CAUGHT

Brother of Negro Killed by Officer Perkinson Locked Up at Second Station.

TO HOLD INQUEST TO-DAY

Post-Mortem Shows That Perkinson's Bullet Killed Relford Pollard.
TO HOLD INQUEST TO-DAY
Thomas Pollard, colored, brother of Relford Pollard, who was shot to death by Policeman Perkinson Saturday night, was arrested yesterday afternoon by Policeman Guy Walker near the house on St. Peter Street where the shooting occurred. He was lodged in the Second Police Station. At the time the police were called in on Saturday night the two Pollards were having a fight over a woman. In the effort to arrest Relford Pollard, Policeman Perkinson found it necessary to shoot him, after the negro had twice hammered the officer over the head with a fence paling. Policeman Walker who had been with Officer Perkinson, chased Tom Pollard for some distance, but the negro made his escape in some dark alleyway, and the officer had since been looking for him.

An inquest will be held over the body of Relford Pollard this morning at 10 o'clock at the City Hall. Coroner William H. Taylor performed an autopsy yesterday morning, tracing the course of the bullet which caused the negro's death. The ball passed crossways almost through the body. It entered the right shoulder, and was extracted from the left side. It passed entirely through the right lung, and severed a large vessel in the heart, and was found bedded in one of the left ribs just under the shoulder.

Denth Instantaneous.

Coroner Taylor has the ball and will compare it with those used in police pistols. According to the account given by Officer Perkinson Saturday night, there had been one or more shots fired in the house between the fighting brothers, and he was not certain whether it had been one of these, or the shot fired by himself at close range in the yard when the negro was attacking him that caused his death. From the nature of the wound, Coroner Taylor thinks there is no doubt but that the policeman's bullet caused death, as from such a wound death would have been almost instantaneous. Furthermore, there was no blood in the house and no drops on the floor to trace where the wounded negro had come out, there being no indication that any of the shots fired in the house took effect Thomas Pollard after his arrest last night said there had been no shooting in the house.
Policeman Perkinson has been bailed for his appearance in the Police Court this morning, but it is expected that the case will be postponed until after hearing the verdict of the coroner's jury.
Examination of Thomas Pollard at the station house last night showed that he had been severely hurt in the side, either in the scuffle with his brother, or more probably in some fall received in jumping fences in his mad dash for liberty when the police officers arrived.
thomas-pollard-richmond-1910-08-21.A5:
POLICE OFFICER IS EXONERATED
W. J. Perkinson Acquitted of Killing Relford Pollard on Grounds of Self-Defense.
Policeman W. J. Perkinson was exonerated yesterday by both the coroner's jury and Justice Crutchfield of the killing of Reiford Pollard, colored, whom he shot after a sharp struggle Saturday night.

The coroner's jury sat for three hours, hearing many witnesses, before bringing in its verdict that the officer shot the negro while in the discharge of his duty. The Police Court hearing was less perfunctory, though the same witnesses were heard, and it was a foregone conclusion that acquittal on the grounds of self-defense would result. Commonwealth's Attorney Folkes conducted the examination for the Commonwealth. Mayor Richardson, Major Werner and Police Commissioners Manning and Gordon were in the courtroom at the time.

Perkinson regarded the proceedings with complete nonchalance. During the coroner's inquest he smoked a cigar and talked with his friends. In Police Court he was no less undisturbed.

Pollard was shot and killed in the rear of 1018 St. Peter Street, where he was engaged in a violent quarrel with his brother, Thomas, when Officers Perkinson and Walker arrived. Both men attempted to escape at the sight of the policemen. Perkinson pursued Reiford Pollard into a backyard, where the negro, according to the officer's statement, turned on him with a paling he had torn from the fence. The officer said he was knocked down twice, and then fired to save himself from injury. The other negro escaped, but was eventually captured, and yesterday morning in Police Court he was placed under $300 bond until his case can be more thoroughly considered.

FIVE HUNDRED ATTEMPTLY FIVE HUNDRED ATTEMPT
COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo., Aug. 14.—As the result of insolence offered Mrs. Alfred Peterson of Denver on a street car in Manitou early tonight, William Johnson, a negro porter of Colorado Springs, was nearly lynched. Nearly 500 excited people of Manitou surrounded the negro, and it was with difficulty that the police finally removed him to a cell in the county jail. Johnson on boarding the car had attempted to hold a double seat. Mrs. Peterson entered after the negro and sat down unintentionally in the seat beside him. A moment later Johnson bodily pushed the woman off the seat so that she fell to the floor of the car.

Aug. 15.—William Johnson and Alva Cornell, colored men, rescued from a mob at Manitou yesterday afternoon, after Johnson had insulted a white woman on a streetcar, are being held for trial on charges of assault and of resisting an officer.

WHICH PRESS DESERVES YOUR SUPPORT.
The daily press went into contortions a few days ago over a possibles lynching in Colorado Springs in which street car manners was the alleged cause. It now appears that no offense was intended nor any taken. Both the colored man and the white woman understood and accepted the situation with no feeling on either side. Outside interference and misunderstanding brought on the bitterness. It is wonderful on what small pretext that lust for blood of Negroes rises. It would have indeed been lamentable had a tragic conclusion come to the matter. In the meanwhile what shall be said of the white press that is such a willing ally of the cussedness shown in this incident? Many of our readers are steady contributors to the support of these papers.
